# Common rules for every catalog task (read fully before editing)

You are a worker on the Teletype data-driven catalog build. The lead wrote the plan; you implement exactly your assigned tasks, test them, and report. The lead verifies and accepts.

## Working directory and build
- Work from your assigned worktree (named in your task file). Never edit the main checkout.
- Export your assigned private `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (named in your task file) before any cargo command. Never share a target dir with another worktree.
- Export `NODE_OPTIONS="--use-system-ca"` for any tooling that needs it.

## Ownership boundary (hard rule)
- You own ONLY the files listed under "Owns" in your task file. Everything else is read-only.
- You may READ any file to understand context. You may WRITE only your owned files.
- If a correct implementation requires changing a file you do not own, STOP and write that in your report. Do not edit it. Do not work around it.
- Do not read other workers' reports, logs, or worktrees.

## Git safety (hard rule)
- NEVER run `git commit`, `git add`, `git push`, `git pull`, `git checkout`, `git restore`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `git clean`, `git rebase`, `git switch`, `git merge`, `git cherry-pick`, `git apply`, or `git am`.
- A git-guard extension blocks ALL git mutations in non-interactive worker sessions. Do NOT try to work around it (no `create_commit` tool, no hooks bypass, no re-running a blocked command). Leave all your work UNCOMMITTED in the worktree.
- The LEAD reads your diff, verifies it, and commits it. Your job ends at a green suite plus a written report, NOT a commit. Any task step that says "commit" is the lead's step, not yours; skip it.
- Read-only git is fine: `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`. To compare against a baseline, read a copy: `git show HEAD:<path> > /tmp/base.rs` and diff against that file.
- If you crash or time out, your partial edits survive; do not revert them on resume.

## Code rules
- No em/en dashes anywhere (code, comments, test names, JSON). Use commas or periods.
- English only everywhere.
- Never write secrets (API keys, tokens). The catalog carries only links, sizes, sha256s.
- Follow the plan's rulings R1-R9 (in the plan's "Plan corrections log"). Cite the ruling id next to edits it drives.
- Default to no comments; add one only for a non-obvious WHY.
- No back-compat shims, no feature flags, no speculative abstraction. Build exactly what the task specifies.

## TDD and test quality
- Follow the plan's red-green steps: write the failing test, run it to confirm it fails for the right reason, implement, run to confirm it passes.
- While iterating, run the focused test for what you changed. Run the full assigned suite ONCE before committing.
- Every new test must contain a real assertion. No assertion-free `debug_*` tests, no scratch probe modules left behind.
- No stray `dbg!`, `eprintln!`, or `println!` in `#[cfg(test)]` code when you finish.
- Report honest before/after test counts. Do not let scaffolding inflate them.
- After adding a struct field, run `cargo clippy --all-targets` for the affected crates (lib-only tests miss integration-test and bench compile errors, and dead fixture fields).

## Verification output (hard rule)
- Paste REAL command output tails and REAL exit codes in your report. Never fabricate or paraphrase a pass.
- Capture the checker's exit code directly: `cmd > out 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?"` then read out. Do NOT pipe into `tail` and report `$?` (that is tail's exit, not the checker's). If you pipe, use `set -o pipefail` and `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`.
- A gate that cannot run in this worktree (e.g. UI tests with no node_modules) is reported as NOT-RUNNABLE, never as a pass.

## Context discipline
- If your context is running low, write your report and stop cleanly rather than crashing mid-edit. A clean partial report beats a crash.
- If you hit the same sub-problem twice without progress, stop and report it; the lead will rule. Do not spin.

## Report
Write your full report to `tasks/pi-reports/<task-id>.md` (path in your task file):
- What you implemented (per task).
- TDD evidence: RED command + failing output, GREEN command + passing output.
- Files changed (git diff --stat).
- Verification commands run with real output tails and exit codes.
- Self-review findings (ownership respected, no debug tests, no em dashes, assertions present).
- Concerns / blockers / out-of-scope changes needed.
Then your final message: Status (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT), files changed (git diff --stat summary, work left uncommitted for the lead), one-line test summary, concerns, report path. Keep the final message under 15 lines; detail lives in the report.

- You own ONLY the files listed under "Owns" in your task file. Everything else is read-only.
- You may READ any file to understand context. You may WRITE only your owned files.
- If a correct implementation requires changing a file you do not own, STOP and write that in your report. Do not edit it. Do not work around it.
- Do not read other workers' reports, logs, or worktrees.

- NEVER run `git commit`, `git add`, `git push`, `git pull`, `git checkout`, `git restore`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `git clean`, `git rebase`, `git switch`, `git merge`, `git cherry-pick`, `git apply`, or `git am`.

- No em/en dashes anywhere (code, comments, test names, JSON). Use commas or periods.
- English only everywhere.
- Never write secrets (API keys, tokens). The catalog carries only links, sizes, sha256s.
